head.h1: Halal Private Dining Catering in Dubai — Prices and What to Ask

opening_paragraph: Halal private dining catering in Dubai, arranged end to end by myCHEF. Halal private dining in Dubai costs about AED 700 to 950 per person for most dinners. A vetted chef plans the menu, sources to halal standards, cooks in your kitchen and serves each course, then leaves the kitchen as it was found. Halal is the default instead of a special request. Send your date, guest count and venue for an itemised proposal.

new_paragraphs: Halal private dining prices in Dubai sit at about AED 700 to 950 per person for most dinners, moving toward the upper end for a table of two and down toward AED 700 for ten or more, because the chef's time spreads across more covers. Tasting menus and multi-course fine dining begin from around AED 1,400 per person. Larger gatherings shift into event pricing with minimums of AED 2,400 or AED 3,600 once staffing and rentals are counted, and every quote carries 5% VAT.

There is no halal premium. What moves the halal private dining cost is the course count, the ingredient tier and whether a server is needed alongside the chef. A shorter menu executed properly eats better than a long one stretched thin, which is also the more economical route. Compare the packages and chef prices before you enquire.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: What's Included in Our Halal Private Dining
new_paragraphs: A chef arrives with the ingredients and the equipment, cooks in your kitchen, serves each course and clears afterwards. For most bookings that is one chef for a table of up to about ten, with a server added for larger groups or a multi-course menu. As a halal private dining catering company, myCHEF handles the sourcing, the menu design, the service and the clean-down, so the evening is yours instead of a project you are managing.

The part that matters to most hosts is sourcing. Meat and poultry come from halal suppliers, alcohol is not used in cooking, and where a classic recipe would normally call for wine or a pork product the dish is rebuilt instead of approximated — a reduction built on stock and vinegar instead of a wine sauce, for example. Your private halal private dining chef will tell you plainly which dishes change and how.

add_block.new_heading: Certification, and what we will and will not claim
new_paragraphs: Halal sourcing and halal certification are different things, and it is worth being precise. Our standard practice is halal sourcing across every menu: suppliers who trade in halal meat and poultry, no alcohol in the cooking, and no cross-use of equipment with non-halal product.

If your event needs documentary certification — a mosque function, a corporate event with a compliance requirement, a family gathering where a guest asks for paperwork — say so when you enquire, and we will confirm in writing what the partner kitchen handling your event can provide before you commit. Telling you the limits up front is better than letting a certificate be assumed and then not produced. The chefs and partner kitchens we work with are licensed in Dubai and operate to the Dubai Municipality Food Code.

add_block.new_heading: The menu, and the occasions it suits
new_paragraphs: The halal private dining menu range is wide, because most cuisines work within halal sourcing without compromise. Arabic and Levantine menus are the natural fit — a Lebanese mezze run of hummus, moutabal, tabbouleh and fattoush, charcoal-grilled meats, slow lamb — but Italian, Indian, Japanese, Mediterranean and modern European menus all run halal without losing their character. Browse the menus or the cuisines for the range, and Arabic catering for the regional depth.

Formats follow the occasion. A seated multi-course dinner suits eight to twelve guests. A family-style spread suits a long table and a relaxed evening. A chef's table suits a smaller, curious group. Ramadan brings its own patterns, with iftar timed to sunset instead of to a convenient hour — see iftar catering and suhoor .

add_block.new_heading: A dinner for two, and other small occasions
new_paragraphs: The smallest bookings are often the ones people care most about. A romantic private dining evening at home — an anniversary, a proposal, a first night in a new apartment — is a normal booking, not an exception squeezed in around bigger ones. The chef works quietly, the courses are paced to the conversation, not to a restaurant's turnover, and the kitchen is left clean. Two guests price at AED 950 to AED 1,300 per person, or the fixed Date Night package from AED 1,200 covers the pair with a three-course menu, service and cleanup.

A small party at home sits just above that: six to twelve people, a family gathering, a birthday, a graduation dinner or the evening before a wedding. It is the same chef and the same halal sourcing, with a server added once the table passes about ten. What changes with size is the menu shape, not the standard — more sharing dishes and fewer individually plated courses, so the food keeps arriving while people are talking.

add_block.new_heading: At home, or a private dining room in a restaurant?
new_paragraphs: If you are weighing affordable private dining rooms in Dubai against a chef at home, the two solve different problems. A restaurant private room gives you a venue, a licence and no clearing up; you accept the house menu, a fixed sitting time and, usually, a minimum spend that is not published anywhere you can check before you call. MyCHEF does not operate restaurant rooms — a private dining room booking is something you take up with the venue directly.

What we arrange is the other route: your own home as the venue, the menu written for your guests, and the halal sourcing settled before anyone cooks. It carries no room hire and no minimum spend, and for a group of ten or more the per-head figure sits at the lower end of the band, from AED 700 and from AED 600 at twenty. Nobody should call it cheap halal private dining — a chef cooking a multi-course menu in your kitchen is a considered purchase, and a quote far below the band usually means fewer hands, thinner sourcing or a shorter menu. The best halal private dining is the booking where the sourcing, the course count and the staffing are all written down before you commit, so the number you agree is the number you pay.

add_block.new_heading: Your kitchen, and how the evening runs
new_paragraphs: A chef needs a working hob, an oven, a clear run of counter for plating, a sink and cleared fridge space. Oven capacity is the real constraint at a seated dinner, because it caps how many mains can leave together — tell the chef about your kitchen and the menu is designed around it. From November to March, when days average around 27°C and nights fall to about 19°C ( Weather and Climate ), a terrace or garden table works comfortably; between May and September, plan indoors.

Guests in Dubai arrive later than the invitation suggests, so give the chef the realistic arrival time instead of the printed one. MyCHEF is implementing a structured partner verification framework covering identity and licence checks, a practical cooking assessment, reference verification and ongoing review after events. Most of these dinners run in villas and apartments in Palm Jumeirah , Emirates Hills , Downtown Dubai and Jumeirah , and the chef travels with everything the menu needs.

new_paragraphs: How much does halal private dining cost in Dubai?
About AED 700 to 950 per person for most dinners, moving toward the upper end for small tables. Tasting menus begin from around AED 1,400 per person. There is no halal premium.
Is halal the default or do I have to request it?
It is the default across our menus. Meat and poultry are sourced from halal suppliers, alcohol is not used in cooking, and equipment is not shared with non-halal product.
Can you provide halal certification documents?

Ask when you enquire and we will confirm in writing what the partner kitchen handling your event can provide before you commit. Halal sourcing is our standard practice; documentary certification depends on the specific kitchen, so we confirm rather than assume.
Which cuisines work as halal private dining?

Most of them. Arabic and Levantine are the natural fit, but Italian, Indian, Japanese, Mediterranean and modern European menus all run halal without losing their character. Recipes needing wine or pork are rebuilt instead of approximated.
How many guests suit private dining?
Eight to twelve is the sweet spot for a seated multi-course dinner with one chef. Smaller suits a chef's table; larger moves into event catering with additional staff.
Do you cater Ramadan iftar and suhoor at home?
Yes. Iftar is timed to sunset instead of to a set hour, which changes the service plan, so those bookings are built around the timing first and the menu second.
Do you do a romantic dinner for two?

Yes, and it is a normal booking, not an exception. Two guests price at AED 950 to AED 1,300 per person, or the fixed Date Night package from AED 1,200 covers the pair with a three-course menu, table service and cleanup.
Do you have private dining rooms in Dubai?

No — a private dining room in a restaurant is booked with the venue directly. What myCHEF arranges is the alternative: a chef cooking a halal menu in your own home, with no room hire and no minimum spend, from AED 700 per person at ten guests.
Do you cover Sharjah and the other emirates?
Coverage is Dubai. Send an address outside the emirate with your enquiry and we confirm before you commit whether it can be served from the Dubai network and what the travel adds to the quote.
What does my kitchen need to provide?

A working hob, an oven, clear counter space for plating, a sink and cleared fridge space. Oven capacity is the main limit on how many hot mains can leave together, so tell the chef about your kitchen early.

add_block.new_heading: Planning halal private dining catering step by step
new_paragraphs: Send your date, guest count and venue — your proposal arrives.
Book a standard private-chef dinner about 48 hours ahead; allow 5 to 7 days for a bespoke menu or a larger table, and 7 to 14 days or more for a wedding, a corporate dinner or Ramadan dates.
Confirm what goes on the menu 7 days out, once the count settles.
Ask for special diets up front; plates are planned, not improvised inside 48 hours .
Check loading and access details; allow 2 hours of setup on site.
Plan on roughly 3 hours of service, and add 5% VAT to the total.

We recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. Booking late for a halal private dining? Send the date first; whether it works depends on which partners are free.
